title: Secret readable just once
body:
### Feature request description

A Podman secret that is given to a container could be marked to allow just one read.
Another attempt to read it would either fail or provide empty or garbled contents.

### Suggest potential solution

For `podman-create` or `podman-run`, add the following sub-options to `--secret`:

- `once+disappear`: remove the environment variable or the file after it is read the first time;
- `once+empty`: set the environment variable or the file empty after it is read the first time;
- `once+garble-ascii`: overwrite the contents of the environment variable or of the file with a random sequence of ASCII characters;
- `once+garble-base64`: overwrite the contents of the environment variable or of the file with a random sequence of bytes encoded as Base64;
- `once+garble-binary`: overwrite the contents of the environment variable or of the file with random bytes.

(Or some other syntax). When overwriting, the garbled contents shall be unique each time a read is attempted. The length should be random, at least a factor of 2–5 of the original length.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Overwriting a secret appears to work for file-mounted secrets if their file modes allow it: an independent podman-exec into the container then sees the overwritten contents. This does not work for a secret passed as an environment variable.

But even that requires the main process in the container to cooperate (=do the overwrite). It would be more secure if the container infrastructure took care of that.

### Additional context

I believe such a feature would improve the secrecy of Podman secrets. They would be used during app initialisation; they would be out of reach if a breach occurs in the operating app.

comments.body:
I don't see how podman can do any of this? Podman has no way of knowing when an env variable was read or when a file was read nor is podman a daemon meaning once the container is started with `podman run -d`  podman exits and has no way of interacting with it in any way.

So really I do not see a way we could do this realistically and I do not think this would be worth it as it sounds rather specific and not something as general purpose.
I don't know how difficult this would be to implement, I'm just suggesting it as a way to make secrets less vulnerable.
